system.summary: Villeroy-office cipher: letters as figures and letter-shaped symbols with homophones, marked letters (comma, one or two dots) for words in alphabetical series, two-digit figures for names and syllables.

diacritics.note: Comma, one dot or two dots on a letter select a word series (f, = le; x, = que; t: = de).

system.doubled_letters: special sign (phi doubles the preceding symbol)
system.sibling_key: Bazeries 1901 prints the 1599 key given to Bethune's brother, same office and design, other values; used for the design only.
system.notes: Known names and words: 48 Cardinal, 17 Aldobrandin, 7 le Roy d'Espagne, 6 (standalone) Sa Saintete; 61 qui, 63 re, 65 si, 66 sa, 68 tout, 71 tion, 72 vous, 73 vostre. 72, 6 and 66 fixed on 14 Nov 2026 from the f. 53r gloss.

prior_solution.where: Halphen 1889 prints the 9 Nov (f. 33) and 22 Nov (f. 46) letters in clear from the originals, by the contributor's record (Brice Dudout, 14 Nov 2026; the print was located here on 22 Oct 2026 and not opened; not seen at integration); clear minute f. 36 for 10 Nov; marginal glosses of other letters. The key was rebuilt on 17 Sept 2026, before the edition was located.

EM alignment of the 10 Nov cipher with its minute plus the glossed passages of 8 Nov and 10 Dec gives the letter values and word signs.
10 Nov letter read in full against the minute.
9 Nov letter decoded with the key and language-model decoders: about six words in ten.
4x re-transcription fixed the doubling sign and the syllable groups 61-73.
Oracle on the known-plaintext blocks: transcription caps decoding at about 71 % of letters; decoder already at the ceiling.
Automatic glyph segmentation and template alignment.
22 Nov letter transcribed in full; clear text read, cipher runs decode to fragments only.
Full-resolution re-reading and figure-split lattice on f. 33; union of two independent readings worth about 2.9 points.
Xivrey, Melanges de Colbert 17, fr. 3677/3678 excluded; Cinq cents de Colbert 346 and Halphen's edition identified, not accessible.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 1107 tokens, 100 types, fr-1600-letters order 4: reading -2.627 per letter; polyphonic: 33% of read tokens differ from their type's commonest value. Verdict: not applicable.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): 10 Nov corpus_v2.txt + reading_10nov.md; 9 Nov ct_f33_v2.txt + decoder output decode_f33_v3/v2 (substance only); 22 Nov reading_22nov.md + ct_22nov.txt (cipher runs decoded only in fragments); key key.tsv

Reading audit (George Lasry's sentence test): reading_10nov.md reads (83% of sentences clean, docs/_check_reading.py, from the clear minute); decode_f33_v3.txt (9 Nov) gives broken lines with nonsense words, and the 22 Nov cipher runs are fragments ('a substance, not a reading'). 9 Nov and 22 Nov relabelled decoded, not read; fraction_read 0.55 -> ~0.2 (estimated).

Re-read (REREAD_BRIEF, b17), step 1: Halphen, Lettres inedites du roi Henri IV a monsieur de Bethune ... du 18 octobre au 24 decembre 1601 (1889) found in full view on HathiTrust (record 100644113, item iau.31858014633857, public domain); babel.hathitrust.org answers with a Cloudflare human-verification page (curl 403; the browser pane shows the checkbox), which this session does not pass. Not on the Internet Archive, Gallica or Google Books (searched). Not on DECODE.

Re-read, step 2: no new image route or transcription; the measured transcription ceiling (oracle 71%, two readers agree on 69% of glyphs, third pass) stands, so the 9 Nov and 22 Nov decodes stay fragments. Both kept decoded, not read; the edition is the route.

Consistency pass (cl): 'read in part' not justified: the Halphen 1889 gap is genuinely untried (not-attempted kept) and the print, key-rebuild and retry escalation steps are not done (left unticked); NOTES Status: in progress. The umbrella gap line for the 9 and 22 Nov runs restated as a lead sentence (its two letters are separate gap lines, mirrored in outcome.gaps).

Verification pass (Claude Opus 5.5): the eight cipher lines of f. 53r block 1 transcribed and aligned with their verbatim marginal gloss (f53r_alignment.md): 72 = vous (four aligned occurrences; settles the earlier proposal and the D1 counter-indication), standalone 6 = Sa Saintete (three), 66 = sa (one), plus 3: = faire, +. = de, n, = nous. Pre-registered check (SHA-256 285ddb07...) on glossed blocks not used for the derivation (f. 56r, f. 50r): one locatable occurrence, agrees; not conclusive; the 200-shuffled-key measurement is not applicable to groups this rare. Three 22 Nov runs give sense (vostre negotiation; correspondance ... discretion; le respect), probable only. Halphen 1889 still behind HathiTrust's human check (403). 9 and 22 Nov stay decoded, not read.

Integration check of pull request #597 (Brice Dudout): the f. 53r alignment compared with the Gallica image (canvas 113, openapi.bnf.fr IIIF, full size), about forty groups of lines 2, 3 and 5-8: 72 seen at the four places the gloss has vous, standalone 6 at the three places it has sa Saincteté, 66 once before volonté; block D1 of f. 49v in corpus_v2.txt already had 'x, d, 72 4 d' under 'que ie vous ay'. The contributor's pre-registered check (n = 1) is not conclusive by its own rule and its declaration is not in the repository (hash only; by the contributor's record). No value changed.

Halphen 1889 (HathiTrust iau.31858014633857) opened by a person in a browser, pp. 8-34: prints the 9 Nov letters (f. 30, f. 33), 10 Nov (f. 34), 18 Nov (f. 38) and 22 Nov (f. 46, from p. 33) from the originals, the ciphered passages given in clear and not marked. Halphen dates the glossed letter ff. 30-31 to 9 Nov (NOTES leaf map: 8 Nov). By the contributor's record.

One pre-registered measurement (PREREG SHA-256 2e3d1707..., script ce5daf65...): frozen key (first value per symbol, no LM) on the whole f. 33 run (970 tokens, ct_f33_v2.txt) against Halphen's clear (1,460 letters), 1 - Levenshtein/max length: 0.507; 200 shuffled keys best 0.291, mean 0.251. Default bar (>= 0.85 and >= best + 0.30) not met; key-signal bar (>= best + 0.15) met. Word classes of the printed text against the decode: 130 sure, 105 probable, 118 restored of 353. Published as failed: the declared bar was not met. Not re-run at integration: neither the declaration, the script nor the printed text is in the repository, so the figures and the order of events are by the contributor's record.

Clear frames of Halphen's text aligned with the decoded runs of f. 33 and f. 46r: 12 = le Grand Duc, 20 = la Seigneurie de Venise, 28 = Espagne, 26 = France, 27 = Italie, 44 = Prince(s), 45 = Duc, 70 = partant; 69 tous?, 67 sans? (halphen_check.md, key.tsv). The frames are the contributor's quotations of the print; 67 and 69 are low and stay open.

Second pre-registered measurement on a fresh portion (PREREG SHA-256 5ad234e5..., key K' = f. 33 key + 12, 20, 26, 27, 28, 44, 45, 67, 69, 70): 34 chunks, 1,062 tokens of ff. 46v-47v and f. 46r l. 31, segmented from the clear frames before decoding, against Halphen pp. 34-40: 0.535; 200 shuffled keys best 0.319, mean 0.276. Default bar not met, key-signal bar met. Strict count on the 371 printed words: 136 sure, 107 probable, 128 restored. (One accidental re-run through an import, fixed seed, same figures.) Published as failed: the declared bar was not met. Not re-run at integration: neither the declaration, the script nor the printed text is in the repository, so the figures and the order of events are by the contributor's record.

Integration check of pull request #603 (Brice Dudout). Halphen 1889 could not be reached here: HathiTrust answers 403 to a script (not got round), archive.org has no copy, the Gallica search answers with its bot check; what it prints is by the contributor's record. The two measurements (0.507 and 0.535 against a declared bar of 0.85) could not be re-run and their hashes could not be recomputed, because the declarations, scripts and reference text are not in the repository: published as failed by the declared bar, with the margin over shuffled keys (best 0.291 and 0.319) stated separately. An own first-value decoder over ct_f33_v2.txt and ct_22nov.txt puts the eight code groups fixed from the print where the quoted phrases need them, next to spelled-out words that agree (r 44 ff g, x Cm r 4 g ff = '. Prince .. mirane' for du Prince de la Mirande; g, p t a ff x 28 = 'la voie . Espagne'; 26 x, B S 28 = 'France que l l Espagne'; 70 72 = 'partant vous'). On the Gallica image of f. 46r (canvas 99) the clear words read 'et pareillement' (l. 10) and 'que Je veux' (l. 24) as the print is quoted, and l. 4 reads 'que des com.ns que Je vous ay faict': reading_22nov.md corrected in these three places from the image. f. 31v (canvas 70) is dated 'le ix.me jour de Novembre': the leaf map's 8 Nov corrected to 9 Nov. Outcome kept at read in part: the printed text of the 9 and 22 Nov letters is not in the repository, the strict share the cipher alone confirms is 0.37 of the printed words on both letters (130 of 353; 136 of 371, the contributor's count), and bringing the text in is a workable gap.

The 10 Nov letter reads (17 cipher lines, about 750 tokens estimated at the 9 Nov letter's 44 tokens a line); the 9 Nov (970 tokens) and 22 Nov (1,879) letters are decoded, not read. About 750 of 3,600, estimated. Unchanged on 14 Nov 2026: Halphen 1889 prints both open letters in clear by the contributor's record, but that text is not in the repository; against it the cipher alone gives 130 sure words of 353 (0.368, 9 Nov) and 136 of 371 (0.367, 22 Nov, the measured runs), the contributor's count. Two pre-registered measurements of the frozen key against that print failed their declared bar (0.507 and 0.535 against 0.85); separately, both stand well above the best of 200 shuffled keys (0.291 and 0.319). Strict sure-word share of the printed words: 0.368 and 0.367. Code groups from the print's quoted frames: 12, 20, 26, 27, 28, 44, 45, 70. codes_open counts the 10 groups without a sure value: 2, 3, 5, 8, 9, 31, 62, 80, and 67 and 69, whose proposed values are low.

texts.label: 10 Nov 1601, f. 34r-v
texts.summary: Henri IV tells Béthune that he paid Cardinal Aldobrandini 10,000 écus through Sillery as a gratification after the Parlement's judgment in the Este-Aldobrandini debt, and will pay 10,000 more in the first months of 1602; Béthune is to tell the Cardinal through Cardinal d'Ossat and pretend not to have received the letter. The cipher is entries A to V3 of corpus_v2.txt (the other entries are glossed passages of the other 9 Nov letter, ff. 30-31, and of the 10 Dec letter); the text comes from the clear minute on f. 36.

reading_review.note: The four cipher passages read from the clear minute f. 36r-v, which gives their full text; continuous French.

texts.note: Decoded, not read here. Halphen 1889, pp. 16-18, prints the whole ciphered passage in clear, by the contributor's record (Brice Dudout, 14 Nov 2026; the edition is on HathiTrust behind a human check, was not seen at integration, and its text is not in the repository). One pre-registered measurement of the frozen key against it scored 0.507 against a declared bar of 0.85: failed; the best of 200 shuffled keys scored 0.291. 130 of the 353 printed words are confirmed by the decode (sure), 105 in part, 118 not at all (the contributor's count, halphen_check.md). The decode stays at the transcription ceiling measured in September (oracle 71% of letters).
texts.label: 9 Nov 1601, f. 33r
texts.summary: A page entirely in cipher. By the contributor's summary of Halphen's print (1889, pp. 16-18): from La Rochepot's secretary in Spain, the King of Spain has taken the Duke of Modena and the Princes of la Mirandola under his protection with pensions on the revenue of Naples and the Golden Fleece; Béthune is to confer with Cardinal Aldobrandini, and the cardinals of Joyeuse and d'Ossat are to advise on Don Alessandro's promotion. The decryption shown is decoder output only; bracketed numbers are open code groups.

texts.note: Decoded, not read here: the clear French reads (reading_22nov.md) but the 80 cipher runs decode only to fragments. Halphen 1889, pp. 33-40, prints the whole letter with the ciphered passages in clear, by the contributor's record (not seen at integration; text not in the repository). A second pre-registered measurement on 1,062 tokens of ff. 46v-47v scored 0.535 against a declared bar of 0.85: failed; best of 200 shuffled keys 0.319. On the 371 printed words of the measured runs 136 are sure, 107 probable, 128 restored from the print (the contributor's count). Three clear-text errors of reading_22nov.md were corrected from the image on 14 Nov 2026 (ll. 4, 10, 24 of f. 46r); others remain to be corrected against the print.
texts.label: 22 Nov 1601, ff. 46r-47v
texts.summary: Henri IV answers Bethune's despatch of 29 October: his negotiation with the Grand Duke and Grand Duchess of Tuscany; Venice and the Grand Duke should have stopped Spain's taking Modena and la Mirandola under its protection; three French candidates for the cardinalate (Evreux, the old Archbishop of Vienne, Clermont); the idea of binding Cardinal Aldobrandini to France with the protection of French affairs; Camaiano's pension; Chateau-Dauphin, Barberini, the Jesuits, the Council; the nuncio in Switzerland; a postscript preferring Clermont to Vienne. Text: Halphen 1889, pp. 33-40.
